# netcheck: down to syscalls

Generated by `codespec-docs` from the checked-in files of [`examples/netcheck`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/tree/main/examples/netcheck). `task examples-netcheck` writes them (Go 1.27.1, linux/amd64, no network); `task check` holds the page to them and checks the facts below.

## The module

`example.com/netcheck` has three packages and imports only the standard library.

| package | what it shows |
|---|---|
| `netcheck` | an interface `Prober` with two implementations: `TCPProber` dials, `FixedProber` does no IO; a generic `Count[T any]` that calls a function value; a variadic `CheckAll`; a function literal; a module variable; `Answer`, which only computes |
| `cmd/server` | entry `main`: `net.Listen`, then `Accept` in a loop, each connection answered with `netcheck.Answer` |
| `cmd/client` | entry `main`: `netcheck.CheckAll(netcheck.TCP(), addr)`, prints how many are up |

```go title="netcheck.go"
// Package netcheck checks whether TCP services answer "ping" with "pong".
package netcheck

import (
	"bufio"
	"io"
	"net"
	"strings"
)

// request is the line a probe sends.
var request = "ping\n"

// Prober tells whether the service at addr is up.
type Prober interface {
	Probe(addr string) bool
}

// TCPProber dials the service and sends "ping".
type TCPProber struct{}

// TCP is a Prober that dials.
func TCP() Prober {
	return TCPProber{}
}

// Probe dials addr, sends "ping" and expects "pong".
func (TCPProber) Probe(addr string) bool {
	c, err := net.Dial("tcp", addr)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	_, werr := io.WriteString(c, request)
	if werr != nil {
		c.Close()
		return false
	}
	line, err := bufio.NewReader(c).ReadString('\n')
	c.Close()
	return err == nil && Answer(line) == "pong"
}

// FixedProber answers from a list of addresses that are up. It does no IO.
type FixedProber struct {
	Up []string
}

// Probe reports whether addr is in the list.
func (p FixedProber) Probe(addr string) bool {
	return Count(p.Up, func(a string) bool { return a == addr }) > 0
}

// Answer is the reply to one request line. It only computes.
func Answer(line string) string {
	switch strings.TrimSpace(line) {
	case "ping":
		return "pong"
	case "":
		return "empty"
	default:
		return "unknown"
	}
}

// Count is how many of xs satisfy ok.
func Count[T any](xs []T, ok func(T) bool) int {
	n := 0
	for _, x := range xs {
		if ok(x) {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// CheckAll probes every address with p and counts those that are up.
func CheckAll(p Prober, addrs ...string) int {
	return Count(addrs, func(a string) bool { return p.Probe(a) })
}
```

```go title="cmd/server/main.go"
// Command server answers each line a client sends with netcheck.Answer.
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"

	"example.com/netcheck"
)

func main() {
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:7070")
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("listen: " + err.Error())
		return
	}
	for {
		c, err := ln.Accept()
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		serve(c)
	}
}

// serve reads one line from c, writes the answer and closes c.
func serve(c net.Conn) {
	line, err := bufio.NewReader(c).ReadString('\n')
	if err == nil {
		io.WriteString(c, netcheck.Answer(line)+"\n")
	}
	c.Close()
}
```

```go title="cmd/client/main.go"
// Command client probes the server and prints how many addresses are up.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"

	"example.com/netcheck"
)

func main() {
	up := netcheck.CheckAll(netcheck.TCP(), "127.0.0.1:7070")
	fmt.Println("up: " + strconv.Itoa(up))
}
```

```text
example.com/netcheck/cmd/server | ok | read 2 of 2 functions, 100.0% | refusals 0
```

No refusal: interfaces, the generic function, the variadic call, the function literal and the module variable are all `cir/1`.

## 2. Effects and syscalls from two entries

```shell-session
$ codespec effects work/netcheck/*.cir.json --barrier summaries/go-linux-amd64.barrier.json \
    --entry example.com/netcheck/cmd/server.main --entry example.com/netcheck/cmd/client.main \
    --report example.com/netcheck --report example.com/netcheck/cmd/server --report example.com/netcheck/cmd/client
```

With entries, dispatch is rapid type analysis (`rta`). The same run with `--dispatch cha` resolves every call through an interface or a function value over the whole set. [`netcheck.effects.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/examples/netcheck/netcheck.effects.json) and [`netcheck.effects-cha.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/examples/netcheck/netcheck.effects-cha.json) hold both reports without `effect_sites`; the `cha` one also without syscall positions.

| function | effects (`rta`) | syscalls `rta` | syscalls `cha` | unknown `rta` |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `netcheck.TCP` | none | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `netcheck.TCPProber.Probe` | `env`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `io`, `net`, `proc`, `time` | 49 | 69 | 5 |
| `netcheck.FixedProber.Probe` | none | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `netcheck.Answer` | none | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `netcheck.Count` | none | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `netcheck.CheckAll` | `env`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `io`, `net`, `proc`, `time` | 49 | 69 | 2 |
| `netcheck/cmd/client.main` | `env`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `io`, `net`, `proc`, `stdout`, `time` | 49 | 69 | 2 |
| `netcheck/cmd/server.main` | `env`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `io`, `net`, `proc`, `stdout`, `time` | 50 | 70 | 10 |
| `netcheck/cmd/server.serve` | `env`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `io`, `net`, `proc`, `time` | 46 | 66 | 3 |

### The entries

The syscalls the barrier maps to `net`, per entry (`rta`):

| syscall | `server.main` | `client.main` |
|---|---|---|
| `accept4` | yes | no |
| `bind` | yes | yes |
| `connect` | yes | yes |
| `getpeername` | yes | yes |
| `getsockname` | yes | yes |
| `getsockopt` | yes | yes |
| `listen` | yes | yes |
| `recvfrom` | yes | yes |
| `sendto` | yes | yes |
| `setsockopt` | yes | yes |
| `socket` | yes | yes |

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| syscalls only the server may reach | `accept4` |
| syscalls only the client may reach | none |
| syscalls both may reach | 49 |

Read a list as *may reach*, not as what a run does. The client only dials, yet `bind` and `listen` are on its list: `net.Dial` goes through `net.socket`, which also binds and listens when it makes a listening socket, and the analysis does not know which branch a run takes.

### The function that only computes

`Answer` calls `strings.TrimSpace` and switches on the result. Read down to the barrier, it has 0 effects, 0 syscalls and 0 `unknown` entries: pure, with nothing over-approximated.

### Dispatch: `rta` against `cha`

Each call through an interface or a function value in the module, and how many functions of the set it may reach:

| function | call | at | `rta` | `cha` |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| `netcheck.TCPProber.Probe` | `net.Conn.Close` | `netcheck.go:35` | 1 | 2 |
| `netcheck.TCPProber.Probe` | `net.Conn.Close` | `netcheck.go:39` | 1 | 2 |
| `netcheck.Count` | `func value func(T) bool` | `netcheck.go:69` | 0 | 0 |
| `netcheck.CheckAll` | `example.com/netcheck.Prober.Probe` | `netcheck.go:78` | 1 | 2 |
| `netcheck/cmd/server.main` | `error.Error` | `main.go:16` | 29 | 44 |
| `netcheck/cmd/server.main` | `net.Listener.Accept` | `main.go:20` | 2 | 2 |
| `netcheck/cmd/server.serve` | `net.Conn.Close` | `main.go:34` | 1 | 2 |

`Prober.Probe` in `CheckAll` reaches only `TCPProber.Probe` under `rta`: no reached code makes a `FixedProber`. `func value func(T) bool` in `Count` has no candidate: a value of a generic signature is a current limit, listed as `unknown`, never taken as pure.

Every `unknown` entry of the module that is not inherited from a callee (`calls … which is incomplete`):

| function | at | reason |
|---|---|---|
| `netcheck.Count` | `netcheck.go:69` | function value with no candidate in the set: func(T) bool |

## 4. Call trees

```shell-session
$ codespec trace work/netcheck/*.cir.json --barrier summaries/go-linux-amd64.barrier.json --from example.com/netcheck/cmd/client.main --depth 2
```

[Call trees](/docs/examples/call-trace#netcheck) draws the client's tree 2 calls deep, and the path from each entry to one syscall: `client.main` to `connect` (16 calls deep), `server.main` to `accept4` (8 calls deep). The full trees are several megabytes; the checked-in [`client-connect.trace.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/examples/netcheck/client-connect.trace.json) and [`server-accept4.trace.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/examples/netcheck/server-accept4.trace.json) keep only the branches that end in that syscall.
